title: Primary-source field audit: evolutionary search and validation for RL environments

questions: How can RL environments, tasks, curricula, rewards, and executable verifiers be generated or evolved?
Which proposed signals already select environments for learnability, realized learning progress, transfer, or diversity?
When is human review necessary, optional, or actively confounding?
What evidence distinguishes executable validity from causal learning value?
Can a small learner validate an environment, and what would support a prospective cross-scale claim?
How should reward hacking, policy-family interactions, and cross-scale rank reversals be detected?
scope.source_policy: Primary arXiv records, official OpenReview records, official proceedings pages, and author-hosted full text linked from an official record were prioritized. Search-result snippets and secondary indexes were used only to locate primary records, not as evidence for scientific claims.
search_surfaces: arXiv current-version API and arXiv abstract/full-text pages
author-hosted full text linked from the primary venue record

evidence_granularity.metadata: The original records were checked against primary sources on 2026-08-23 and the canonical union, exact arXiv versions, and additions were reconciled on 2026-08-24. Every primary URL and version date is current through the stated cutoff.
evidence_granularity.scientific_claims: Every relationship and difference is limited to a claim visible in the exact-version primary abstract or inspected full text. The full texts of the two closest performance-gain competitors, the marginal-benefit AAAI paper and All Life is Problem Creation, were inspected directly; selected method and limitation sections of DEGen, the UED optimisation framework, verifier-gaming work, and TRACED v5 were also inspected. The TRACED audit verified its one-step shadow correlations and its stated long-horizon oscillation boundary directly from the paper.
evidence_granularity.negative_search_claim: After expanding and deduplicating the three scoped landscapes into a canonical union of 85 primary records, no checked paper directly matched the complete surviving conjunction. This is a bounded audit inference over the stated search and source set, not a proof that no such work exists.

occupied_components: Evolutionary co-generation of environments and policies is established by POET and Enhanced POET.
Regret-guided, replay-guided, mutation-based, diffusion-based, and dynamically generated UED curricula are established by PAIRED, PLR, Dual Curriculum Design, ACCEL, ADD, DEGen, and related work.
Joint task-and-level generation is occupied by CoDE and ATLAS.

Quality-diversity archives, learned behavioral descriptors, procedural-content RL, evolutionary simulator task diversity, and multi-agent environment design are established by MAP-Elites, AURORA, PCGRL, DIVA, and MAESTRO. Diversity or archive illumination is not proof of open-endedness, and retraining a learned descriptor can move archive cells.

Autotelic and automatic curricula based on goal difficulty, absolute learning progress, setter-solver feasibility and coverage, self-paced distributions, and massive open-ended task universes are established by GoalGAN, ALP-GMM, Setter-Solver, Self-Paced DRL, TeachMyAgent, and XLand.

Selecting environments using learner-local signals is occupied by value disagreement, SFL learnability, marginal benefit, parameter-change magnitude, success bands, novelty, improved regret approximations, transition-prediction error, and TRACED Co-Learnability.
Optimizing a generator on measured target-task performance gain is occupied by MBeED/MBeDED and, more directly, All Life is Problem Creation.

Executable environment and verifier synthesis, factored heterogeneous environment generation, small-model GameCWM generation, solve-verify asymmetry, staged validation, adaptive difficulty, and post-hoc gains at multiple model sizes are occupied by OMNI-EPIC, AutoEnv, EnvFactory, GameCWM, RLVE, SCALER, Endless Terminals, RLAnything, Agent-World, EvoEnv, Envs-FORGE, and SPADE.

Zero-data task self-play and verifier-backed proposal are occupied by Absolute Zero, R-Zero, Propose-Solve-Verify, Verifier-Backed Hard Problem Generation, Agentic Self-Learning, and AutoPlay; autonomous task generation is not the surviving novelty.

Hidden performance functions, causal reward tampering, reward-model overoptimization, capability-dependent reward misspecification, embedded hack opportunities, verifier-gaming perturbation tests, and learned-exploit contamination and persistence are established evaluation components.

Smooth RL scaling for selected objectives and recipes is established, while architecture-sensitive scaling, reward-hacking thresholds, and small-run data-ranking reversals show why model size or one fixed training recipe is not a valid fidelity axis.
executive_verdict.exact_surviving_conjunction: Generate or inherit executable environment families, but make the contribution a preregistered causal-value measurement protocol. Freeze one deduplicated union candidate pool, separate randomized absolute-learnability and allocation-value estimands, the 1,080-cell discovery/calibration lattice, ordered max-t procedure, resource rule, horizons, predictor, eight-candidate promotion roster, and top-k selection using discovery-only policies, a logged development outcome, and a development exploit suite. Then open independently implemented immutable confirmation outcomes and independently authored natural and planted exploit suites exactly once across 60 target cells per candidate that separately identify family, optimizer, and joint shifts. None of the 85 primary records checked here directly combines prospective causal-value prediction, this confirmation boundary, learned-exploit persistence tests, and explicit multi-fidelity falsification.
executive_verdict.novelty_boundary: The defensible novelty is not environment generation, quality-diversity, autotelic or open-ended learning, adaptive difficulty, Co-Learnability, realized learning-progress scoring, zero-data task self-play, executable verification, or post-hoc gains at several model sizes. It is prospective falsification of whether cheap evidence predicts causal environment value and exploit resistance outside the learner, generator, verifier, and fidelity used for selection.

most_material_new_findings.finding: Marginal Benefit Driven RL Teacher for Unsupervised Environment Design already trains a teacher using the return difference between an updated and slightly outdated student, then evaluates zero-shot transfer. Any claim to be the first to score environments by realized learning improvement is untenable.

All Life is Problem Creation already trains a proposer on the solver's measured performance gain over held-out target tasks and conditions generation on solver probes. Its narrow maze study does not test a sealed, untouched target fidelity or cross-family calibration, but it directly occupies target-performance-gain environment generation.
DEGen and Maximised Negative Advantage strengthen both learned generation and regret approximation, so original PAIRED or PLR scores alone are inadequate baselines.

ATLAS mutates and selects task-level pairs, so evolving only level layouts cannot be framed as broad environment evolution. The genome must explicitly distinguish task specification, transition system, reward, termination, and evaluator.

Isomorphic Perturbation Testing shows a concrete metamorphic route for detecting verifier-passing shortcuts. A generic exploit-policy panel should include semantics-preserving perturbations, not only known attack trajectories.

TRACED directly models cross-task Co-Learnability, so curriculum interaction is not a novel signal. Its v5 shadow test reports Pearson 0.3998 and Spearman 0.2013 for one-step temporal consistency, while its 45k-update single-seed runs oscillate; it is a baseline, not a long-horizon causal certificate.

MAP-Elites establishes archive-based quality-diversity, while AURORA establishes learned behavioral descriptors and their dependence on representation choice. An illuminated or drifting archive cannot by itself support an open-endedness or learning-value claim.

Reward-model overoptimization depends on optimization method, KL, reward-model data, and model scale. Exploit validation therefore needs explicit optimization and inference fidelity axes plus a hidden outcome, not one undifferentiated exploit percentage.

Small-run data-recipe rankings can flip under minor hyperparameter changes. A cross-scale environment selector must compare tuned or explicitly crossed training fidelities and simple frozen rank baselines before claiming added predictive value.

AutoEnv factorizes transition, observation, and reward distributions and shows that fixed learning methods lose effectiveness as heterogeneous environment count grows. Together with EnvFactory and GameCWM, it makes broad environment automation and small-generator feasibility occupied components; none of the three supplies prospective candidate-level causal-value calibration at an untouched fidelity.

Countdown-Code v2 reports that low-rate hacked-trajectory contamination can teach reward hacking that reappears during RL and generalizes beyond the contaminated task. Exploit auditing must therefore cover trajectory provenance, controlled contamination, post-RL recurrence, mitigation recurrence, and cross-domain persistence.

feasibility_review.reason: Use 5.9 because the canonical 85-record audit preserves the narrow causal-value and immutable-confirmation conjunction but the identifiable design now requires a fixed 1,152-cell pilot and 9,120-cell main study before baseline pipelines. Do not open confirmation unless the pilot gives at least 80 percent power and the frozen GPU-hour ceiling funds the complete design.

Retain 6.6 as an implementation-oriented within-scale gate, but define certificate as an empirical evidence packet rather than a formal guarantee. MBeED, All Life is Problem Creation, PACE, TRACED Co-Learnability, causal reward-tampering tests, reward-model overoptimization, Hack-Verifiable Environments, and verifier-gaming tests must be explicit baselines or components. The package is novel only as a randomized causal-invariance, delayed-retention, and immutable-hidden-outcome gate.

Use 6.1. The audit found strong analogues for RL scaling, small-run selection, Co-Learnability, architecture-dependent ranking, optimizer-dependent proxy divergence, and learned exploit persistence, but no direct prospective candidate-environment selection-regret study with independent confirmation outcomes and exploit suites. The identifiable design requires 1,140 cells for each of eight promoted candidates after a fixed 1,152-cell pilot.

human_in_the_loop.answer: Humans are not scientifically necessary in every generation, verification, or training loop. Fully autonomous pipelines can generate and filter tasks without per-task annotation when semantics and success are captured by independent executable checks. Human review remains justified for choosing the target capability distribution, auditing open-ended semantics and unknown exploits, and estimating correlated validator blind spots. It should not become the primary outcome or an unlogged source of reward shaping.
evidence: Endless Terminals explicitly reports a fully autonomous, no-human-annotation generation pipeline and transfer to human-curated terminal benchmarks.
EvoEnv uses staged executable validation and semantic self-review; this supports automation in formal reasoning domains but does not prove that self-review catches unknown semantic failures.
OMNI-EPIC models human notions of interestingness with foundation models, illustrating that open-ended interestingness is not the same property as formal task validity.
RLVE's 400 environments were manually engineered, showing that current strong results also rely on substantial human environment design rather than proving it is intrinsically required.
human_in_the_loop.recommended_experiment: Split review into a pre-training construct-and-safety gate and a post-selection blind audit. Before policy training, review every new semantic or high-consequence family and a pilot-powered random sample of automation-accepted and automation-rejected candidates. After selection freezes, use a fresh sentinel sample and compare automation-only, targeted, equal-budget uniform, and exhaustive review under one rubric. Measure minutes, stage, reversals, false-negative intervals, agreement, planted-exploit recall, and double-blind natural-failure discovery. Keep human judgments out of mutable fitness.
human_in_the_loop.decision_rule: Omit routine human review only if the automation-only excess-failure upper bound is below the registered tolerance. If targeted routing fails its secondary superiority or noninferiority test, fall back to the safer registered uniform or exhaustive policy; do not erase an otherwise passing causal-value result merely because targeted routing failed.

what_counts_as_learning_signal.answer: Executable validity, solvability, intermediate success rate, regret, novelty, parameter change, or one positive learning curve is not sufficient. Claim useful learning signal only after estimating two distinct interventions on the inaccessible confirmation outcome: absolute learnability against resource-matched no-update exposure and allocation value against a randomized eligible-pool replacement.
what_counts_as_learning_signal.minimal_causal_contrast: Randomly assign blocked curriculum runs among base curriculum plus candidate, base plus resource-matched no-update exposure, and base plus a replacement sampled from the preregistered eligible pool within family, difficulty, and resource blocks. Match environment interactions and learner compute; log optimizer steps, effective KL, update norm, tokens, verifier calls, wall time, GPU-hours, and human minutes. State the replacement positivity population, treat curriculum runs as inferential units, cluster by lineage and family, and measure immediate and prefrozen delayed confirmation outcomes that generation and discovery cannot query.
what_counts_as_learning_signal.attribution_caveat: Environment value can be non-additive. Make randomized blocked add-one effects primary and compare TRACED Co-Learnability as a predictor. Report budgeted Shapley-style estimates only as exploratory interaction summaries, never as exact attribution when coalition coverage is sparse.
screening_signals: regret and improved regret approximations such as MNA
marginal benefit between pre-update and post-update policies
what_counts_as_learning_signal.interpretation: These are candidate predictors and allocation signals. Their scientific value comes from prospective calibration against the causal held-out effect, not from their intuitive appeal.

must_a_model_be_trained.answer: No model training is required to reject mechanically invalid, unreachable, nondeterministic, reward-inconsistent, or known-exploitable environments. Some training intervention is required to claim useful learning signal. It need not be a small model specifically: a small model is a cost-saving screen, not a logical prerequisite.
must_a_model_be_trained.minimum_for_learning_claim: Use a pilot-powered intervention with at least two learning recipes at the same declared fidelity. For stochastic environments, pair frozen-policy repeated rollouts with coupled seeds and no-update versus update arms so aleatoric drift is not mislabeled as learning. A single short run can triage candidates but cannot establish robust learning value, delayed retention, transfer, or scaling.

small_model_proxy_and_scaling.answer: A gain for one small model supports only a within-recipe screening statement. A scaling claim requires a prospective prediction made before the target run. Post-hoc gains across several related sizes, as reported by current environment-synthesis systems, do not by themselves establish calibration or stable environment ranking.
small_model_proxy_and_scaling.discovery_design: Per promoted candidate use 1,080 discovery/calibration cells: three smaller capacities by three interaction budgets by three policy-and-RL-algorithm families by two optimizers by two inference budgets by two tool regimes by five coupled seeds. Manipulate those six factors; match and log optimizer steps, effective KL, update norm, tokens, and FLOPs. A fixed 1,152-cell pilot on eight pilot-only candidates excluded from the main union precedes the study and must provide at least 80 percent power and a GPU-hour ceiling that funds all 9,120 main cells.
small_model_proxy_and_scaling.untouched_target: Promote exactly eight candidates—two top, one bottom, two ambiguous, and three uniformly random. Before target training, freeze the union pool, feature extraction, value predictor, max-t family, resources, hyperparameter transfer rule, horizons, promotion roster, intervals, exploit thresholds, and success criteria. For each candidate open 60 target cells at a fourth capacity and interaction budget: held-out family with known optimizer, known family with held-out optimizer, and their joint shift, crossed with two inference budgets, two tool regimes, and five seeds. Score them once with inaccessible confirmation outcomes and exploit suites.
small_model_proxy_and_scaling.ordered_decision: Use simultaneous one-sided max-t intervals for target selection-regret improvement against every eligible selector, followed in order by allocation value, absolute learnability, delayed retention, held-out-family regret, held-out-optimizer regret, joint-shift regret, interval calibration, and exploit resistance. Kendall tau-b, pairwise accuracy, and Jaccard are diagnostic unless separate pilot-derived utility margins and multiplicity-adjusted thresholds are frozen. Human-routing efficacy is secondary and chooses the review fallback rather than entering this core family.
required_metrics: causal marginal area-under-learning-curve uplift on the sealed neutral suite
Kendall tau-b and pairwise sign accuracy across fidelities as diagnostics unless pilot-derived utility margins and multiplicity-adjusted gates are registered
top-k selection regret against the expensive target ranking as primary; top-k overlap is descriptive
sign-reversal rate only for effects whose confidence intervals lie beyond the practical-equivalence margin
binomial-uncertainty-aware prediction-interval coverage, weighted interval score, and sharpness
held-out-family selection regret and conditional ranks
reward-to-hidden-evaluator divergence and exploit success as optimization power increases
small_model_proxy_and_scaling.failure_interpretation: If rankings reverse beyond the practical margin, report conditional environment value by learner family instead of averaging to a universal score. If mean gain rises but target selection regret, delayed retention, interval undercoverage, or exploit gates fail, the scaling claim fails. Overcoverage alone is reported with sharpness rather than automatically rejected. A rigorously negative rank-transfer result remains a valid contribution.

design: Permit a mutable, fully logged development outcome and development exploit suite on discovery only. Keep an independently implemented immutable confirmation evaluator and independently authored natural and planted confirmation exploit suites outside the mutable genome and deny the generator, agent, reward code, and discovery process direct or side-channel access.
Run random, scripted, known-good, known-bad, known-hack, and search-based adversarial policies.
Embed held-out hack opportunities that are verifiable by design, while retaining a separate natural exploit suite so success is not limited to planted attacks.
Apply semantics-preserving isomorphic and metamorphic transformations; reward and success should remain invariant while shortcut outputs fail.

Cross capacity, interaction budget, policy/algorithm family, optimizer, inference budget, and tool access because capability thresholds can reveal exploits absent in weak agents; treat optimizer steps, effective KL, update norm, tokens, and FLOPs as matched diagnostics.

Version solver, SFT, and distillation trace provenance; cross clean and controlled low-rate planted-hack contamination arms, then test post-RL recurrence, post-mitigation recurrence, and persistence on a held-out environment family.

Audit evaluator implementation overlap, hashes, query budgets, timing, logs, network access, and other side channels; version every reward, test, solver, evaluator, exploit family, container, and evaluator interaction.
reward_hacking_and_exploit_audit.blocking_rule: Define exploit opportunity units, denominators, severity strata, and hierarchical confidence intervals before testing. A simple zero-event one-percent upper-bound claim needs roughly 300 independent opportunities. Block promotion when the joint minimum-effect confidence region permits reward to rise while the hidden outcome falls materially, the planted-exploit superiority or natural-failure noninferiority test fails, or controlled trajectory contamination produces material post-RL recurrence or cross-domain persistence.

required_brief_corrections.correction: Acknowledge Marginal Benefit Driven RL Teacher and All Life is Problem Creation in the motivation, novelty assessment, competitor landscape, and baselines. Replace any implication that realized or target-task performance-gain scoring is new.

Add MBeED/MBeDED, Proposer (Performance Gain), DEGen plus MNA, PACE, SFL, TRACED Co-Learnability, and the simplest small-learner rank as mandatory value-selection baselines. Add ATLAS when both task specifications and levels are mutable.

State that discovery may query a mutable logged development outcome and development exploit suite, but confirmation uses an independently implemented immutable evaluator and independently authored natural and planted exploit suites that generation and discovery cannot access. Freeze the union pool, estimands, predictor, resources, ordered max-t family, horizons, eight-candidate roster, and top-k before opening confirmation once. Merely resampling target instances is not sufficient separation.

Define the environment genome as separately typed task specification, instance generator, transitions, observations/actions, reward, termination, solver, and visible tests. Keep the hidden evaluator and exploit suite immutable and outside mutation.
Clarify that a learning-signal certificate is an empirical evidence packet, not a proof of universal validity. Reserve formal certificate language for properties actually guaranteed by a verifier.
Add isomorphic perturbation testing and planted hack-verifiable opportunities to the exploit audit, while retaining natural unknown-exploit sentinels.

Split review into a pre-training construct-and-safety gate and a fresh post-selection blind audit, each with random accepted/rejected sentinels powered from pilot prevalence. Compare automation-only, targeted, uniform, and exhaustive review. Keep routing efficacy secondary and use the safer registered fallback if it fails; do not state that humans are categorically required or unnecessary.

Run the fixed 1,152-cell pilot on eight pilot-only candidates excluded from the main union, require at least 80 percent power for the minimum useful allocation effect, and freeze the absolute GPU-hour ceiling, five main seeds, baseline costs, and exchange rates before main runs. Promote exactly eight different candidates and fund all 9,120 main cells or keep confirmation closed. Publish interactions, FLOPs, tokens, verifier calls, wall time, GPU-hours, and human minutes.

Use randomized blocked add-one effects at the curriculum-run level as primary attribution, with lineage and family clustering. Compare TRACED Co-Learnability and report budgeted Shapley values only as exploratory interaction summaries. Carry a random candidate sample to full fidelity to quantify adaptive-pruning bias.
Keep the cross-scale package separate from within-scale validity. No within-scale reward, optimizer, or checkpoint intervention should be described as evidence that an environment scales.

Freeze one deduplicated union candidate pool before comparing value selectors. Evaluate native POET, ACCEL, learned-generator, LLM, and self-play pipelines separately as end-to-end systems; do not attribute pool differences to selector quality.

For stochastic environments, use frozen-policy repeated rollouts, coupled seeds, and no-update versus update arms to separate aleatoric drift from learning. Freeze immediate and delayed-retention horizons before training.

Audit confirmation-evaluator and confirmation-exploit-suite implementation overlap, hashes, query budgets, timing, logs, network access, and other side channels. Target leakage, post-unblinding tuning, familywise-procedure changes, or any confirmation evaluator or exploit-suite update blocks the claim immediately.

Split discovery, calibration, and target data jointly by generator lineage, prompt or level template, normalized program AST, and semantic capability family. Random instance splits do not establish contamination control.

Use 1,080 discovery/calibration cells per promoted candidate: three capacities by three interaction budgets by three policy/algorithm families by two optimizers by two inference budgets by two tool regimes by five seeds. Treat optimizer steps, effective KL, update norm, tokens, and FLOPs as matched diagnostics. Add 60 target cells at a fourth capacity and budget that separately identify held-out family, held-out optimizer, and their joint shift.

Make target-tier selection regret primary and compare every eligible selector with simultaneous one-sided max-t intervals. Order later gates as allocation value, absolute learnability, delayed retention, held-out-family regret, held-out-optimizer regret, joint shift, calibration, and exploit resistance. Keep tau-b, pairwise accuracy, and Jaccard diagnostic unless pilot-derived utility margins and multiplicity-adjusted gates are frozen.

Define exploit opportunity units, denominators, severity strata, and hierarchical intervals. Test planted-exploit superiority and natural-failure noninferiority separately, plus a joint reward-up/hidden-down confidence region. Add trace provenance, controlled low-rate planted-hack contamination, post-RL and post-mitigation recurrence, and held-out-family persistence tests following Countdown-Code v2.

Use the ordered familywise hierarchy: no leakage, executable validity, immediate allocation value and absolute learnability, delayed retention, simultaneous target selection regret, separately identified held-out-family and held-out-optimizer regret, interval calibration, then exploit resistance. Human routing is secondary; invalid-candidate rate is a generator cost unless it leaks into selection or target evaluation.

Bound conclusions to registered domain and semantic families. MAP-Elites, quality-diversity coverage, and learned behavioral descriptors do not prove open-endedness; descriptor retraining can create archive drift.

primary_sources.title: AI Safety Gridworlds
primary_sources.difference: It separates observed reward from a hidden performance function in hand-designed safety tests. It supplies the evaluator separation principle but does not generate environments, measure their marginal training value, or calibrate rankings across scale.

primary_sources.title: Paired Open-Ended Trailblazer (POET): Endlessly Generating Increasingly Complex and Diverse Learning Environments and Their Solutions
primary_sources.difference: POET co-evolves environments and specialist policies and transfers stepping stones. It occupies evolutionary environment search, but it does not prospectively predict candidate-level causal transfer to unseen learner families or audit hidden-outcome divergence.

primary_sources.title: Enhanced POET: Open-Ended Reinforcement Learning through Unbounded Invention of Learning Challenges and their Solutions
primary_sources.difference: Enhanced POET strengthens open-ended invention, characterization, and transfer. Its target is open-ended complexity and solution discovery, not an independently sealed environment-value validator.

primary_sources.title: Automatic Curriculum Learning through Value Disagreement
primary_sources.difference: Value disagreement proposes goals near the policy's reachability frontier using epistemic uncertainty. It is a cheap learner-local selection signal, not a causal downstream effect or cross-scale predictor.

primary_sources.title: Prioritized Level Replay
primary_sources.difference: PLR prioritizes levels using learner-derived estimates such as temporal-difference error and improves procedural generalization. It does not synthesize full semantics or validate candidate value on a generator-inaccessible outcome and untouched scale.

primary_sources.title: Emergent Complexity and Zero-shot Transfer via Unsupervised Environment Design
primary_sources.difference: PAIRED generates structured, solvable environments by maximizing protagonist-antagonist regret and evaluates zero-shot transfer. Regret is therefore a mandatory baseline, but no prospective cross-family value calibration or exploit audit is provided.

primary_sources.title: Learning Synthetic Environments for Reinforcement Learning with Evolution Strategies
primary_sources.difference: It evolves neural proxy environments using target-task performance in the outer loop and explicitly tests hyperparameter and algorithm transfer, finding limited transfer in some cases. It makes learner invariance a required test; the remaining delta is executable open-ended families, sealed outcomes, exploit auditing, and prospective scale calibration.

primary_sources.title: Replay-Guided Adversarial Environment Design
primary_sources.difference: Dual Curriculum Design unifies generation and replay and provides equilibrium robustness results. The audited program instead tests finite-training causal neutral-suite effects and whether candidate rankings survive learner and fidelity shifts.

primary_sources.title: The Effects of Reward Misspecification: Mapping and Mitigating Misaligned Models
primary_sources.difference: It shows that more capable agents can raise proxy reward while lowering true reward and can cross qualitative capability thresholds. It directly rules out weak-agent reward agreement as an environment certificate, but does not search or rank training environments.

primary_sources.title: Environment Generation for Zero-Shot Compositional Reinforcement Learning
primary_sources.difference: CoDE trains a generator to build compositional tasks tailored to the student's current skill and evaluates zero-shot generalization. It occupies learner-adaptive task composition but not sealed marginal attribution or prospective scale prediction.

primary_sources.title: Evolving Curricula with Regret-Based Environment Design
primary_sources.difference: ACCEL mutates replayed levels toward the learner's frontier using regret. It must be reproduced under common budgets; its objective does not prospectively calibrate candidate value across policy families, target scale, and exploit strength.

primary_sources.title: Scaling Laws vs Model Architectures: How does Inductive Bias Influence Scaling?
primary_sources.difference: It reports that relative architecture performance can fluctuate with scale. The implication here is methodological: environment value cannot be treated as learner-independent without explicit environment-by-architecture interactions and family holdouts.

primary_sources.title: Scaling laws for single-agent reinforcement learning
primary_sources.difference: It derives smooth intrinsic-performance relationships in studied environments. It predicts performance for a fixed environment family and recipe, not the relative causal value of generated training environments.

primary_sources.title: Mixtures of Experts Unlock Parameter Scaling for Deep RL
primary_sources.difference: The work shows that dense parameter scaling and architecture choice interact in deep RL. It motivates treating architecture and optimization family as separate fidelity axes rather than using parameter count as the sole definition of scale.

primary_sources.title: OMNI-EPIC: Open-endedness via Models of human Notions of Interestingness with Environments Programmed in Code
primary_sources.difference: OMNI-EPIC generates environment and reward code chosen for learnability and modeled human interestingness. It occupies open-ended code generation; it does not isolate a hidden evaluator, compute causal downstream value, or freeze a cross-scale predictor.

primary_sources.title: Discovering Minimal Reinforcement Learning Environments
primary_sources.difference: It searches minimal synthetic environments and improves invariance across algorithms and hyperparameters, including contextual-bandit proxies for MDP evaluation. It narrows novelty for cross-agent synthetic proxies but does not address open-ended executable semantics, sealed exploit outcomes, or prospective unseen-scale ranking.

primary_sources.title: No Regrets: Investigating and Improving Regret Approximations for Curriculum Discovery
primary_sources.difference: It finds failures in practical regret approximations and proposes SFL to select learnable binary-outcome tasks. SFL is a mandatory baseline, but intermediate success remains a within-learner proxy rather than sealed causal transfer or scale calibration.

primary_sources.title: Value-Based Deep RL Scales Predictably
primary_sources.difference: It predicts data-compute frontiers and scale-dependent hyperparameters for several value-based algorithms and domains. It is a design template for a frozen extrapolation test but does not predict candidate-environment effects or rankings.

primary_sources.title: Improving Environment Novelty Quantification for Effective Unsupervised Environment Design
primary_sources.difference: CENIE measures novelty through state-action coverage and combines it with regret. It makes generic diversity claims non-novel; coverage must be treated as a candidate predictor and ablated against causal transfer.

primary_sources.title: DataDecide: How to Predict Best Pretraining Data with Small Experiments
primary_sources.difference: DataDecide studies which small experiments predict data choices and warns that simple ranking rules can beat elaborate scaling-law fits. Smallest-learner and mean-rank baselines are therefore mandatory for ScaleFalsifier.

primary_sources.title: Marginal Benefit Driven RL Teacher for Unsupervised Environment Design
primary_sources.difference: MBeED trains a teacher on the return difference between an updated student and a slightly outdated copy in the generated environment; MBeDED adds representative-state diversity and the paper evaluates zero-shot transfer. This occupies marginal-benefit environment scoring. It does not use a generator-inaccessible neutral-suite effect, a cross-family holdout, or a prospectively frozen target-scale predictor.

primary_sources.title: An Optimisation Framework for Unsupervised Environment Design
primary_sources.relationship: theoretical and practical UED optimization competitor
primary_sources.difference: It formulates UED as nonconvex-strongly-concave optimization, provides convergence results for the zero-sum setting, and implements a practical dynamic-buffer algorithm. It raises the optimization baseline but does not estimate sealed candidate-level causal value across unseen learners and scale.

primary_sources.title: All Life is Problem Creation: Learning to Generate Environments that Maximize Performance Gain
primary_sources.source_version: SEA @ NeurIPS 2025 Poster; OpenReview record modified 2025-11-19
primary_sources.difference: The proposer is conditioned on solver behavior and rewarded by the solver's measured gain on randomly sampled held-out target tasks after an inner training loop. This directly occupies performance-gain curriculum generation. The inspected study uses one solver recipe, one maze domain with two narrow distributions, five runs, and repeated access to the target distribution; it does not freeze a predictor for an untouched scale or family, audit exploits, or demonstrate stable candidate rankings.

primary_sources.title: RLVE: Scaling Up Reinforcement Learning for Language Models with Adaptive Verifiable Environments
primary_sources.difference: RLVE adapts difficulty within 400 manually engineered verifiable environments and reports generalization gains. It makes adaptive difficulty and larger environment pools non-novel, but it does not autonomously search new families or prospectively calibrate each candidate's marginal value at an unseen fidelity.

primary_sources.title: Beyond Fixed Tasks: Unsupervised Environment Design for Task-Level Pairs
primary_sources.source_version: arXiv:2511.12706v2; AAAI 2026 proceedings version also checked
primary_sources.difference: ATLAS generates solvable, challenging task-level pairs and mutates both reward-machine tasks and MiniGrid levels. It occupies joint task/level evolution but does not measure candidate causal value on a sealed outcome or test cross-scale and cross-family rank stability.

primary_sources.title: GenEnv: Difficulty-Aligned Co-Evolution Between LLM Agents and Environment Simulators
primary_sources.difference: GenEnv conditions generation on learner capability and targets a useful difficulty band. Its success alignment is a direct baseline; it does not establish that success-band scores predict compute-matched neutral transfer, exploit resistance, or cross-family target ranking.

primary_sources.title: SCALER:Synthetic Scalable Adaptive Learning Environment for Reasoning
primary_sources.difference: SCALER creates verifiable reasoning environments, adapts instance difficulty, and retires saturated environments. The remaining delta is a frozen predictor of causal marginal value across policy families and unseen fidelity, not maintaining frontier difficulty.

primary_sources.title: Improving Regret Approximation for Unsupervised Dynamic Environment Generation
primary_sources.relationship: closest current learned-generator and regret-objective baseline
primary_sources.difference: DEGen supplies denser teacher credit assignment and Maximised Negative Advantage improves challenging-level identification as environments grow. It must be included as a strong generator and score baseline; it does not test generator-inaccessible causal transfer or prospective scale ranking.

primary_sources.title: Endless Terminals: Scaling RL Environments for Terminal Agents
primary_sources.difference: It reports a fully autonomous pipeline generating and validating 3,255 terminal tasks without human annotation and transfer to human-curated benchmarks. This disproves any blanket need for per-task human review in formal domains, but does not adapt generation to learner feedback or estimate candidate-level causal value.

primary_sources.title: RLAnything: Forge Environment, Policy, and Reward Model in Completely Dynamic RL System
primary_sources.difference: RLAnything jointly updates tasks or environments, policy, and reward feedback. It occupies broad joint adaptation, while its coupled signals motivate the audited program's stricter requirement that the hidden outcome remain independent and sealed.

primary_sources.title: BeamPERL: Parameter-Efficient RL with Verifiable Rewards Specializes Compact LLMs for Structured Beam Mechanics Reasoning
primary_sources.difference: BeamPERL reports that continued exact-reward optimization can maintain reward while topological robustness deteriorates. It does not generate environments, but it directly shows why verifier correctness and one learning curve cannot certify transferable learning signal.

primary_sources.title: LLMs Gaming Verifiers: RLVR can Lead to Reward Hacking
primary_sources.difference: It finds RLVR models can exploit extensional verification and proposes Isomorphic Perturbation Testing to distinguish genuine rules from shortcuts. The audited program should incorporate this test family, then add environment generation, independent hidden outcomes, and stronger-policy prospective auditing.

primary_sources.title: Agent-World: Scaling Real-World Environment Synthesis for Evolving General Agent Intelligence
primary_sources.difference: Agent-World synthesizes executable tool ecosystems and capability-targeted tasks. It narrows autonomous discovery and co-evolution claims, but it does not prospectively calibrate candidate-level causal value or hidden-outcome exploit risk across policy families.

primary_sources.title: PACE: Parameter Change for Unsupervised Environment Design
primary_sources.difference: PACE scores an environment through a first-order approximation to the policy-parameter update and reports strong MiniGrid and Craftax OOD results. It directly occupies realized local learning-progress scoring; the remaining question is whether the score predicts sealed causal transfer for unseen learners and fidelity.

primary_sources.title: Learning to Build the Environment: Self-Evolving Reasoning RL via Verifiable Environment Synthesis
primary_sources.difference: EvoEnv synthesizes executable reasoning environments and uses staged validation, semantic self-review, solver-relative calibration, novelty, and solve-verify asymmetry. Another generate-filter loop is not novel; the audited delta is an independent causal and cross-scale environment-value test.

primary_sources.title: Hack-Verifiable Environments: Towards Evaluating Reward Hacking at Scale
primary_sources.difference: It embeds detectable hacking opportunities in environments for deterministic measurement at scale. The audited program should use it as an exploit-audit component but adds evolutionary selection, natural unknown-exploit sentinels, causal learning value, and target-fidelity prediction.

primary_sources.title: Reward Hacking in Language Model Agents: Revisiting AI Safety Gridworlds
primary_sources.relationship: cross-scale negative evidence on proxy reward
primary_sources.difference: It reports observed-versus-hidden objective gaps that persist across 1.5B to 14B models and widen under direct reward optimization. This supports stronger-optimizer exploit holdouts; it evaluates fixed safety tasks rather than candidate training-environment value.

primary_sources.title: Envs-FORGE: Frontier-Optimized Reward-Grounded Environment Synthesis for Agent RL
primary_sources.difference: Envs-FORGE uses verifier-derived pass rates and a per-seed optimization to choose difficulty or diversity rewrites, then reports gains across Qwen 4B to 35B. It makes frontier targeting and post-hoc multi-size gains non-novel; it does not freeze a candidate-value predictor or test calibration, marginal effects, and exploit gaps at an unseen scale and family.

primary_sources.title: SPADE: Self-Play in Adaptive Synthetic Executable Environments
primary_sources.difference: SPADE trains an environment designer through privileged-hint regret and reports gains up to 30B parameters. Adaptive executable synthesis is therefore occupied. The surviving question is whether a frozen cheap predictor identifies compute-matched causal value and exploit resistance across unrelated learner families when regret gives the wrong ordering.

primary_sources.title: Illuminating search spaces by mapping elites
primary_sources.difference: MAP-Elites maps high-performing solutions across user-chosen dimensions. It is a foundational archive and search baseline, but an illuminated archive is neither proof of open-endedness nor evidence that its members cause downstream learning.

primary_sources.title: Automatic Goal Generation for Reinforcement Learning Agents
primary_sources.difference: GoalGAN adversarially proposes goals near the learner's current competence and builds an automatic curriculum. It occupies intermediate-difficulty goal generation but does not estimate generator-inaccessible causal transfer or prospective scale stability.

primary_sources.title: Autonomous skill discovery with Quality-Diversity and Unsupervised Descriptors
primary_sources.difference: AURORA replaces handcrafted behavioral descriptors with unsupervised dimensionality reduction. It makes descriptor learning established while exposing a measurement risk: retraining the representation can move archive cells without genuine behavioral progress.

primary_sources.title: Reward Tampering Problems and Solutions in Reinforcement Learning: A Causal Influence Diagram Perspective
primary_sources.difference: This work formalizes when agents have instrumental incentives to tamper with reward functions or reward inputs and gives causal design principles. It supplies the tamper-surface model but not generated-environment value or cross-fidelity validation.

primary_sources.title: Automated curricula through setter-solver interactions
primary_sources.difference: Setter-Solver explicitly balances goal validity, feasibility, and coverage in rich sparse-reward domains. These are established generation gates, but they do not identify compute-matched causal transfer on an inaccessible outcome.

primary_sources.title: Teacher algorithms for curriculum learning of Deep RL in continuously parameterized environments
primary_sources.difference: ALP-GMM treats task selection as a continuous bandit and targets absolute learning progress for an initially unknown student. It is a mandatory learner-local baseline, not a sealed causal-value or cross-scale predictor.

primary_sources.title: PCGRL: Procedural Content Generation via Reinforcement Learning
primary_sources.difference: PCGRL frames level design as an MDP and learns fast content generators without example corpora. It occupies RL-based environment-content generation, while the proposed audit asks whether generated training exposure causes sealed transfer.

primary_sources.title: Self-Paced Deep Reinforcement Learning
primary_sources.difference: Self-Paced DRL learns a distribution over tasks that approaches a target distribution at a pace set by the agent. It is a strong curriculum baseline but does not validate new executable semantics, hidden outcomes, or an untouched target fidelity.

primary_sources.title: TeachMyAgent: a Benchmark for Automatic Curriculum Learning in Deep RL
primary_sources.difference: TeachMyAgent supplies challenge-specific unit tests, procedural environments, and a comparative ACL study. It is an evaluation substrate for curriculum methods, not evidence that one candidate-value score transfers across policy families or scale.

primary_sources.title: Open-Ended Learning Leads to Generally Capable Agents
primary_sources.difference: XLand changes task distributions and objectives across a massive multi-agent universe and measures iterative agent improvement. It establishes broad open-ended curriculum training but not candidate-level causal attribution or a frozen unseen-fidelity selector.

primary_sources.title: Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization
primary_sources.difference: This work measures proxy-versus-gold reward divergence under RL and best-of-n and varies KL, policy and reward-model size, and reward-model data. It makes optimization and inference fidelity explicit exploit axes; it does not generate or select environments.

primary_sources.title: Generalization through Diversity: Improving Unsupervised Environment Design
primary_sources.difference: DRED uses a task-relevant environment distance to avoid redundant high-learning-potential selections and improves OOD generalization. It directly occupies diversity-aware UED but not generator-inaccessible causal transfer or target calibration.

primary_sources.title: MAESTRO: Open-Ended Environment Design for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
primary_sources.difference: MAESTRO constructs joint curricula over environments and co-player policies with minimax-regret guarantees in two-player zero-sum settings. It occupies multi-agent UED but does not prospectively calibrate candidate value across unseen policy families.

primary_sources.title: Enabling Adaptive Agent Training in Open-Ended Simulators by Targeting Diversity
primary_sources.difference: DIVA evolves diverse training tasks in complex open-ended simulators for adaptive meta-RL agents. It makes evolutionary task diversity in realistic simulators non-novel; it does not use an immutable target evaluator or prospective causal-value ranking.

primary_sources.title: Absolute Zero: Reinforced Self-play Reasoning with Zero Data
primary_sources.difference: Absolute Zero trains one model to propose and solve verifier-backed code and math tasks without external data and reports compatibility across scales and model classes. Autonomous task generation and post-hoc multi-scale gains are occupied; prospective candidate-value calibration is not.

primary_sources.title: TRACED: Transition-aware Regret Approximation with Co-learnability for Environment Design
primary_sources.difference: TRACED combines transition-prediction error with Co-Learnability, an observational estimate of how selecting one task changes difficulty on replayed tasks. Its v5 shadow test reports Pearson 0.3998 and Spearman 0.2013 one step ahead, and the paper reports single-seed long-horizon oscillations for TRACED and ACCEL. It is a mandatory baseline, not causal attribution or delayed-retention validation.

primary_sources.title: R-Zero: Self-Evolving Reasoning LLM from Zero Data
primary_sources.difference: R-Zero co-evolves separate Challenger and Solver models to generate frontier tasks without pre-existing labels. It occupies self-generated curriculum construction but does not keep a confirmation evaluator inaccessible or test causal candidate rankings across fidelity.

primary_sources.title: Scaling Synthetic Task Generation for Agents via Exploration
primary_sources.difference: AutoPlay explores interactive application states before generating executable, verifiable agent tasks and reports post-training gains without human task annotation. It occupies grounded task generation at scale but not candidate-level causal attribution or unseen-fidelity calibration.

primary_sources.title: Towards Agentic Self-Learning LLMs in Search Environment
primary_sources.difference: Agentic Self-Learning co-evolves a prompt generator, policy, and generative reward model and reports that a frozen verifier can induce reward hacking. It occupies joint adaptation while motivating a stricter independent immutable confirmation outcome.

primary_sources.title: Propose, Solve, Verify: Self-Play Through Formal Verification
primary_sources.difference: Propose-Solve-Verify uses formal verification to train a difficulty-aware problem proposer and solver without human data. It occupies reliable verifier-backed self-play in code, but not multi-fidelity causal environment-value prediction.

primary_sources.title: Can Small Training Runs Reliably Guide Data Curation? Rethinking Proxy-Model Practice
primary_sources.difference: This work shows data-recipe rankings from small runs can flip under minor training-hyperparameter changes and argues that recipes should be compared under their own tuning. It requires explicit optimization fidelity and simple rank baselines in any small-to-large environment selector.

primary_sources.title: Verifier-Backed Hard Problem Generation for Mathematical Reasoning
primary_sources.difference: VHG adds a verifier to setter-solver self-play so proposer reward combines validity and difficulty. It occupies verifier-backed hard-problem generation but does not use a sealed neutral outcome, randomized marginal attribution, or cross-fidelity candidate calibration.

primary_sources.title: AutoEnv: Automated Environments for Measuring Cross-Environment Agent Learning
primary_sources.relationship: heterogeneous cross-environment generation and adaptation competitor
primary_sources.difference: AutoEnv factorizes transition, observation, and reward distributions, builds 36 environments with 358 validated levels, and shows that fixed learning methods lose effectiveness as environment diversity grows. It occupies heterogeneous environment generation and adaptive learning selection but not prospective candidate-level causal-value calibration at an untouched fidelity.

primary_sources.title: EnvFactory: Scaling Tool-Use Agents via Executable Environments Synthesis and Robust RL
primary_sources.difference: EnvFactory automatically explores and verifies 85 stateful tool environments across seven domains and synthesizes grounded multi-turn SFT and RL trajectories with downstream gains. It makes automated tool-environment construction non-novel but does not freeze a causal-value selector or generator-inaccessible target evaluator.

primary_sources.title: Distilling Game Code World Model Generation into Lightweight Large Language Models
primary_sources.difference: GameCWM distills structural and semantic game-code generation into Qwen2.5-3B with SFT and RLVR over 30 games. It shows that a small generator can improve mechanical environment validity, but it does not test whether generated environments cause transferable learning value.

primary_sources.title: Leveraging Procedural Generation to Benchmark Reinforcement Learning
primary_sources.difference: Procgen establishes procedurally varied training and held-out-level evaluation across sixteen environments. It is a required generalization substrate but does not evolve full environment semantics or prospectively calibrate candidate causal value.

primary_sources.title: Learning Synthetic Environments and Reward Networks for Reinforcement Learning
primary_sources.difference: This work evolves neural proxy dynamics and reward networks, evaluates multiple algorithms, and reports transfer to unseen agents. It occupies joint environment and reward evolution but not inaccessible confirmation or prospective target-fidelity selection.

primary_sources.title: Grounding Aleatoric Uncertainty for Unsupervised Environment Design
primary_sources.difference: SAMPLR shows adaptive curricula can exploit aleatoric variables and induce harmful covariate shift. The audited protocol must ground irreducible factors to deployment and separate stochastic drift from learning.

primary_sources.title: Same Pre-training Loss, Better Downstream: Implicit Bias Matters for Language Models
primary_sources.difference: Models can share pretraining loss yet differ downstream because training dynamics and implicit bias differ. This supports matched-proxy controls and explicit optimizer interactions rather than treating one loss as environment value.

primary_sources.title: Stabilizing Unsupervised Environment Design with a Learned Adversary
primary_sources.difference: This work stabilizes learned-adversary UED and raises the generator baseline beyond original PAIRED. It does not prospectively predict causal environment value across unseen family, optimizer, and scale.

primary_sources.title: Eureka: Human-Level Reward Design via Coding Large Language Models
primary_sources.difference: Eureka evolves executable reward code and can incorporate human feedback while dynamics remain fixed. It occupies reward-only evolution but not full environment-family search with inaccessible confirmation outcomes.

primary_sources.title: Refining Minimax Regret for Unsupervised Environment Design
primary_sources.difference: ReMiDi addresses regret stagnation and is a stronger UED objective baseline. It does not estimate allocation value on an inaccessible confirmation outcome or target-tier selection regret.

primary_sources.title: EnvGen: Generating and Adapting Environments via LLMs for Training Embodied Agents
primary_sources.difference: EnvGen adapts simulator configurations to observed weak skills and improves small embodied agents. It occupies learner-conditioned environment adaptation but not inaccessible exploit confirmation or prospective unseen-family calibration.

primary_sources.title: LLM-POET: Evolving Complex Environments using Large Language Models
primary_sources.difference: LLM-POET uses language-model mutations in Evolution Gym. It is a direct generator baseline but does not establish causal allocation value or stable candidate ranking across unseen learner factors.

primary_sources.title: Adversarial Environment Design via Regret-Guided Diffusion Models
primary_sources.difference: ADD guides a diffusion generator using regret and diversity. It raises learned-generation baselines but does not use a one-time confirmation outcome, separate causal estimands, or held-out optimizer tests.

primary_sources.title: The Art of Scaling Reinforcement Learning Compute for LLMs
primary_sources.difference: ScaleRL distinguishes compute efficiency from asymptotic performance with sigmoidal curves. It informs capacity-by-experience modeling but does not rank generated environments prospectively.

primary_sources.title: WebGym: Scaling Training Environments for Visual Web Agents with Realistic Tasks
primary_sources.difference: WebGym supplies a large realistic task pool and reports held-out-site transfer. It establishes environment breadth at scale but not candidate-level causal allocation or unseen-family calibration.

primary_sources.title: Agent World Model: Infinity Synthetic Environments for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
primary_sources.difference: Agent World Model scales database-backed tool environments and synthetic RL. It raises scale and reliability baselines but does not freeze a causal-value selector for untouched family and optimizer contrasts.

primary_sources.title: ReSyn: Autonomously Scaling Synthetic Environments for Reasoning Models
primary_sources.difference: ReSyn generates reasoning environments with instance generators and verifiers. It occupies autonomous scalable synthesis but not randomized allocation effects or one-time exploit confirmation.

primary_sources.title: Countdown-Code: A Testbed for Studying The Emergence and Generalization of Reward Hacking in RLVR
primary_sources.difference: Countdown-Code reports that hacked SFT traces can induce reward hacking that resurfaces during RL and generalizes beyond the contaminated task. It makes trace contamination, recurrence, and cross-domain persistence mandatory exploit axes.

primary_sources.title: Nexus: Same Pretraining Loss, Better Downstream Generalization via Common Minima
primary_sources.difference: Nexus provides current evidence that similar proxy loss can hide different downstream solutions. It motivates matched-small-proxy environment pairs but is not an environment generator or selector.

primary_sources.title: CUA-Gym: Scaling Verifiable Training Environments and Tasks for Computer-Use Agents
primary_sources.difference: CUA-Gym co-generates tasks, states, and deterministic rewards at scale. It occupies automated verifiable environment construction but not prospective causal-value ranking with inaccessible confirmation.

primary_sources.title: Explaining Data Mixing Scaling Laws
primary_sources.difference: This work models how mixture composition changes scaling. It supports explicit curriculum-interaction and conditional-value modeling but does not study evolved RL environments.

primary_sources.title: EurekAgent: Agent Environment Engineering is All You Need For Autonomous Scientific Discovery
primary_sources.difference: EurekAgent treats permissions, artifacts, budgets, and human intervention as environment-engineering primitives. It informs sandboxing and oversight but does not evolve RL environment families or calibrate their causal learning value.

primary_sources.title: From Trainee to Trainer: LLM-Designed Training Environment for RL with Multi-Agent Reasoning
primary_sources.difference: The current checkpoint diagnoses failure trajectories and edits the next training environment configuration. It occupies learner-conditioned redesign but not randomized allocation value or untouched family and optimizer validation.

primary_sources.title: Can Transformers Really Do It All? On the Compatibility of Inductive Biases Across Tasks
primary_sources.difference: This work studies incompatibility among task-specific inductive biases. It supports explicit held-out policy-family testing rather than a universal environment ranking but does not generate or select RL environments.

audit_limitations: The field is moving quickly; papers submitted after the cutoff or records not indexed by the searched primary systems are outside scope.

A primary abstract was sufficient for inclusion only when the relationship and difference did not require a result hidden in the body. The two closest performance-gain papers and TRACED's exact temporal-consistency and long-run claims were inspected in full because their objectives or quantitative boundaries determine novelty and design.
Several 2026 systems are arXiv technical reports or works in progress. Their claims are treated as occupied empirical components, not as settled general laws.
No claim of universal absence is made. The surviving-conjunction statement is explicitly bounded to the canonical union of 85 primary records in this audit and the search surfaces above.
